questions.prompt: If the envoy were present, he would explain the whole affair to us.
questions.answer: Sī lēgātus praesēns esset, tōtam rem nōbīs explicāret.

questions.prompt: If you were telling the truth, we would not seek another excuse.
questions.answer: Sī vērum dīcerēs, aliam excūsātiōnem nōn peterēmus.

questions.prompt: If the soldiers were braver, they would not fear the approaching enemy.
questions.answer: Sī mīlitēs fortiōrēs essent, hostem adpropinquantem nōn timērent.

questions.prompt: If I had enough time, I would untie this difficult knot.
questions.answer: Sī satis temporis habērem, hunc difficilem nōdum solverem.

questions.prompt: If the general had arrived sooner, he would have saved the ancient city.
questions.answer: Sī dux mātūrius vēnisset, urbem vetustam servāvisset.

questions.prompt: If you had obeyed the old man, you would not have made this mistake.
questions.answer: Sī senī pāruissēs, hunc errōrem nōn fēcissēs.

questions.prompt: If they had recognized the danger, they would have fled at once.
questions.answer: Sī perīculum cognōvissent, statim fūgissent.

questions.prompt: If the poet had lived longer, he would have written many praiseworthy books.
questions.answer: Sī poēta diūtius vīxisset, multōs librōs laudābilēs scrīpsisset.

questions.prompt: Since night was already falling, the travelers sought a lodging.
questions.answer: Cum nox iam caderet, viātōrēs hospitium petēbant.

questions.prompt: When the storm was raging, the sailors did not dare to leave the harbor.
questions.answer: Cum tempestās saevīret, nautae portum relinquere nōn audēbant.

questions.prompt: Since he was suffering from a grave illness, the king summoned a physician.
questions.answer: Cum gravī morbō labōrāret, rēx medicum arcessīvit.

questions.prompt: While the enemy were pressing hard, our men bravely defended the wall.
questions.answer: Cum hostēs vehementer urgērent, nostrī mūrum fortiter dēfendēbant.

questions.prompt: When the consul had spoken these words, the whole senate fell silent.
questions.answer: Cum cōnsul haec verba dīxisset, tōtus senātus conticuit.

questions.prompt: Since the gates had been closed, the citizens were unable to escape.
questions.answer: Cum portae clausae essent, cīvēs effugere nōn poterant.

questions.prompt: When the general had drawn up his battle line, he gave the signal for combat.
questions.answer: Cum dux aciem īnstrūxisset, signum proeliī dedit.

questions.prompt: After the messenger had reported the victory, the people rejoiced greatly.
questions.answer: Cum nūntius victōriam nūntiāvisset, populus magnopere laetātus est.

questions.prompt: The general sent scouts to learn the enemy's plans.
questions.answer: Dux explōrātōrēs mīsit ut hostium cōnsilia cognōscerent.

questions.prompt: We hurried so that we might not interrupt the sacred rites.
questions.answer: Properāvimus nē sacra interrumperēmus.

questions.prompt: The mother was afraid that her son would never return home.
questions.answer: Māter verēbātur nē fīlius numquam domum redīret.

questions.prompt: The teacher explained everything clearly so that the boys might understand.
questions.answer: Magister omnia clārē explicāvit ut puerī intellegerent.

questions.prompt: I asked the old woman why she had abandoned her homeland.
questions.answer: Rogāvī anum cūr patriam relīquisset.

questions.prompt: No one knew where the fleet had sailed during the night.
questions.answer: Nēmō sciēbat quō classis nocte nāvigāvisset.

questions.prompt: So great was the uproar that no one could hear the leader's voice.
questions.answer: Tantus erat tumultus ut nēmō vōcem ducis audīre posset.

questions.prompt: He chose brave men to carry the difficult order into the camp.
questions.answer: Dēlēgit fortēs virōs quī difficile mandātum in castra ferrent.

questions.prompt: If the barbarians were besieging the city, the citizens would defend the walls bravely.
questions.answer: Sī barbarī urbem oppugnārent, cīvēs mūrōs fortiter dēfenderent.

questions.prompt: If the king had heard the truth, he would have spared the conquered enemy.
questions.answer: Sī rēx vērum audīvisset, hostī victō pepercisset.

questions.prompt: If you were thirsting, I would offer you cold water from the spring.
questions.answer: Sī sitīrēs, tibi aquam frīgidam ē fonte offerrem.

questions.prompt: If the most famous orator had been present, he would have swayed the whole crowd.
questions.answer: Sī ōrātor clārissimus adfuisset, tōtam turbam mōvisset.

questions.prompt: Since the soldiers had been exhausted by the long march, the leader granted a rest.
questions.answer: Cum mīlitēs longō itinere dēfessī essent, dux quiētem concessit.

questions.prompt: When the fleeing enemy had thrown away their weapons, our men ceased from slaughter.
questions.answer: Cum hostēs fugientēs arma abiēcissent, nostrī ā caede dēstitērunt.

questions.prompt: Although the wound was bloody, the brave veteran concealed his pain.
questions.answer: Cum vulnus cruentum esset, veterānus fortis dolōrem cēlābat.

questions.prompt: When the funeral had been completed, the mourners returned to the city.
questions.answer: Cum fūnus cōnfectum esset, maerentēs in urbem revertērunt.

questions.prompt: The bald merchant hid the gold lest the thieves find it.
questions.answer: Mercātor calvus aurum cēlāvit nē fūrēs id invenīrent.

questions.prompt: The general fortified the camp so that the barbarians could not break through.
questions.answer: Dux castra mūnīvit nē barbarī perrumpere possent.

questions.prompt: They offered a sacrifice so that the gods would grant a favorable outcome.
questions.answer: Sacrificium obtulērunt ut deī secundum ēventum concēderent.

questions.prompt: The mother sent her son away so that he might avenge his father's death.
questions.answer: Māter fīlium dīmīsit ut mortem patris ulcīscerētur.

questions.prompt: The judge asked why the accused man had fled from the city.
questions.answer: Iūdex rogāvit cūr reus ex urbe fūgisset.

questions.prompt: We did not know how great a danger threatened the sleeping soldiers.
questions.answer: Nesciēbāmus quantum perīculum mīlitibus dormientibus impendēret.

questions.prompt: The old man related how the ancient temple had been destroyed by fire.
questions.answer: Senex nārrāvit quōmodo templum antīquum igne dēlētum esset.

questions.prompt: It was uncertain whether the wavering allies would keep faith.
questions.answer: Incertum erat num sociī īnstābilēs fidem servārent.

questions.prompt: So great was the storm that the sailors despaired of their life.
questions.answer: Tanta erat tempestās ut nautae dē vītā dēspērārent.

questions.prompt: The commander feared that the wavering battle-line would give way.
questions.answer: Imperātor timēbat nē aciēs īnstābilis cēderet.

questions.prompt: The citizens were afraid that the cruel tyrant had already seized power.
questions.answer: Cīvēs verēbantur nē tyrannus crūdēlis iam potestātem occupāvisset.

questions.prompt: When the deed had been done, the assassin fled into the shadows.
questions.answer: Cum factum patrātum esset, sīcārius in tenebrās fūgit.

questions.prompt: The scouts advanced quietly so that they might explore the enemy's camp.
questions.answer: Explōrātōrēs tacitē prōcessērunt ut castra hostium explōrārent.

questions.prompt: I often wondered why the modest farmer had refused such great wealth.
questions.answer: Saepe mīrābar cūr agricola modicus tantās dīvitiās recūsāvisset.
